what: Security: v2's CLI connects with blaze_api::client::Client::unix (cli/daemon.rs:61,90), which never checks who serves the socket: a second user who can make <BLAZE_HOME>/v2.sock (a shared or 0777 BLAZE_HOME, a stale XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) gets the user's request and environment. v1's client refused (`the peer is user N`, crates/blaze-cargo/src/socket.rs check_peer, which the v2 path does not use). Port: Client::unix checks the peer's uid against getuid (SO_PEERCRED / getpeereid as socket/unix.rs peer_user) and refuses with `the peer is user N`. harness/blaze_cli.py's stranger check is ported to v2 (BLAZE_HOME at a socket a second user serves, then `blaze status`) and fails until this lands.
